note: Prepared from the unit title and the trade's usual practice. An instructor must read and correct it, and mark it Ready, before it is opened for an intake.

unit.title: Perform testing and inspection of electrical installations

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: Before the initial verification of a new two-storey house, which information should the inspector collect?
options: Only the client's receipts for all the materials bought
Drawings, circuit schedule, design data and device ratings
The builder's programme for the painting and tiling work
The power bills for the last year from the previous owner

questions.stem: What does initial verification confirm about a new installation?
options: It meets the design and standard and is safe to switch on
It was finished by the date written in the builder's contract
The client is happy with where every switch was placed
The cheapest materials allowed were used throughout

questions.stem: Why is a periodic inspection of an older hotel's installation carried out?
options: To redesign it in line with the latest fashion in fittings
To check that the power company's meter reads correctly
To find damage, wear and changes that affect safety
To replace every cable that is more than five years old

questions.stem: Before a periodic inspection of an occupied office, why must the extent and limitations be agreed with the client and written down?
options: So the inspector can leave out any circuit he finds hard
So the client knows how much each test will cost in J$
So the power company can plan when to read the meter
So everyone knows what will and will not be inspected

questions.stem: During a periodic inspection you open a sample of outlets and find several loose terminals. What should you do?
options: Stop sampling, since the rest are likely to be fine
Tighten them and leave them out of the report
Open a bigger sample, as more faults are likely
Record a pass, because loose terminals are not a danger

questions.stem: Which defect can be found only by inspection, and not by the usual dead tests?
options: A break in the protective conductor of a circuit
An insulation fault between line and earth in a cable
A single-pole switch connected in the neutral
An outdoor fitting with the wrong IP rating

questions.stem: When inspecting a house, where on the incoming metal water pipe do you expect to find the main bonding clamp?
options: At the far end of the pipe, in the last bathroom
As close as practical to its point of entry
Anywhere on the pipe, then painted over to protect it
On a plastic section, where it is easier to reach

questions.stem: What does the IP rating on a light fitting for a pool deck tell the inspector?
options: How well it keeps out solid objects and water
How many watts of lamp it can safely take
Which maker built it and in which country
How long its lamp should last before it fails

questions.stem: You find a 2.5 mm² cable protected by a 40 A breaker on a general outlet circuit. What should you record?
options: Nothing, because a larger breaker trips less often
A pass, as long as the insulation test result is good
An improvement, to be done at the next inspection
A defect: the breaker does not protect the cable

questions.stem: A distribution board has an empty breaker space with no blank fitted. Why is this recorded as a defect?
options: It lets dust in, which can make the breakers trip
Fingers or tools can reach live parts through the gap
It means the board was bought from the wrong maker
The power company will not read the meter until it is fixed

questions.stem: Which label should an inspector expect at a board fed by both the mains and a standby generator?
options: A warning that the board has more than one supply
A label that gives the generator's purchase price
A notice listing all the electricians' phone numbers
A sign telling users to switch each breaker monthly

questions.stem: When inspecting a house with a standby generator, what must the inspector confirm about the changeover arrangement?
options: The generator is fed in through an outlet with a two-plug lead
The generator is larger than the house's total connected load
It cannot connect the generator and the mains together
The changeover switch is fitted outdoors beside the meter

questions.stem: On a new installation, which tests are done before the supply is connected?
options: Continuity, insulation resistance, polarity and earth electrode
Earth fault loop impedance and RCD trip time, and no others
Prospective fault current and phase sequence, and no others
Functional tests of every switch and appliance, and no others

questions.stem: The cable data gives 19.5 mΩ per metre for line plus protective conductor. What should R1 + R2 be for a 40 m circuit?
Ze at the origin is 0.35 Ω, and R1 + R2 for a circuit is 0.78 Ω. What is the expected earth fault loop impedance (Zs) at the end of that circuit?
A breaker needs 100 A to trip instantly, and the line-to-earth voltage is 110 V. What is the largest loop impedance that still lets it trip instantly?
Why is a measured loop impedance compared with a figure lower than the maximum in the table?
options: Test instruments always read about half the true value
Conductors heat up in a fault, so their resistance rises
The table's values are only for direct current circuits
The supply voltage is higher at night than during the day

questions.stem: Ze at the origin is 0.4 Ω, and the line-to-earth voltage is 110 V. What is the prospective earth fault current?
Why must the prospective fault current at a distribution board be known?
options: To work out how many outlets each circuit may have
To set the voltage on the insulation resistance tester
To check that each device can safely break that current
To decide the colour of the cables used in the board

questions.stem: Three circuits each read 300 MΩ when tested alone. Tested together at the board, they read about 100 MΩ. What does this show?
options: One of the three circuits has developed an earth fault
The tester's battery was going flat during the last test
The board's main switch was left open during the test
Nothing is wrong: circuits in parallel read lower

questions.stem: Before an insulation test of a whole board, what should be done with a surge protective device fitted in it?
options: Leave it in place, since it will help to raise the reading
Short it out with a wire link for the length of the test
Disconnect it, or follow the maker's test instructions
Remove its earth wire and leave it disconnected for good

questions.stem: Which of these is a functional test, done once the supply is on?
options: Measuring the insulation resistance of each cable
Measuring R1 + R2 on each of the final circuits
Testing the earth rod with two test spikes
Operating each switch, isolator and interlock

questions.stem: When a competent person tests a 30 mA RCD at half its rated current (15 mA), what should happen?
options: It should trip within a few milliseconds
It should not trip at all
It should trip only after a full minute
It should trip and then reset by itself

questions.stem: After the RCD tests, why is the user shown the RCD's own test button?
options: So they can check, at set times, that it still trips
So they can reset the breakers whenever they trip
So they can measure the leakage on each circuit
So they can turn off the whole supply each night

questions.stem: A measured Zs is higher than the maximum allowed for the circuit's breaker. What could this mean if an earth fault happens?
options: The breaker will trip much faster than it needs to
The RCD will trip every time a lamp is switched on
The circuit's insulation reading will be too high
The breaker may not trip fast enough to clear it

questions.stem: What is a correct way to deal with a circuit whose Zs is too high for its breaker?
options: Fit a breaker with a higher current rating instead
Look for poor joints, then the designer decides a fix
Remove the protective conductor to stop the readings
Record it as a pass, if the circuit works normally

questions.stem: A building's earth rod has a higher resistance than the design allows. What is most likely to lower it?
options: Drive the rod deeper, or add rods spaced apart
Paint the top of the rod to stop it from rusting
Use a thinner earthing conductor to the rod
Move the rod into dry sand close to the building

questions.stem: On a three-phase board, between which conductors is the insulation test made?
options: Line 1 to earth only, as the others are the same
Neutral to earth only, with the lines left floating
All lines and neutral to each other and to earth
Line 1 to line 2 only, as the rest are much alike

questions.stem: Which document is issued when an electrician adds one outlet to an existing circuit?
options: A short certificate for minor works
A periodic condition report
A full certificate for a new installation
A power company meter request

questions.stem: On the certificate for a new building's installation, whose signatures confirm the design, the construction, and the inspection and testing?
options: The client, the architect and the power company
The building's owner and the hardware supplier
The people responsible for each of those stages
Only the apprentice who did most of the wiring

questions.stem: During a periodic inspection you find an outlet with live parts that can be touched. How should it be classed?
options: Improvement recommended, at the next inspection
No action needed, as long as it carries a label
Potentially dangerous, to fix within a few months
Danger present: make safe now and tell the client

questions.stem: A periodic inspection finds one item classed as potentially dangerous. What overall result should the report give?
options: Satisfactory, since the other circuits are all fine
Unsatisfactory, until that item has been put right
Satisfactory, as long as the client signs the report
No result, because that circuit was out of scope

questions.stem: What decides the interval to the next periodic inspection that the inspector recommends?
options: The client's choice, based on what they want to spend
The type of use, the condition found and the setting
Always the same: every twenty years for any building
The age of the inspector's own test instruments

questions.stem: In Jamaica, who must inspect and approve a new installation before the power company will connect it?
options: The government electrical inspector
The power company's meter reader
The architect who drew the building
The municipal corporation's fire officer

questions.stem: In a busy supermarket, you must isolate circuits that feed freezers and tills. What should you arrange first?
options: Switch off quickly before the staff can object
Tell the staff afterwards which circuits went off
Agree times with the manager so stock and data are safe
Leave those circuits out of the tests without a note

questions.stem: As lead inspector, you check a trainee's schedule and see the same continuity reading, 0.10 Ω, on circuits of very different lengths. What should you do?
options: Sign it, since a steady figure shows careful testing
Change some figures so the schedule looks more real
Ask the client whether the figures look right to them
Check the trainee's method and retest a sample yourself

questions.stem: Why does the inspector check a sample of terminations for tightness on a new installation?
options: Tight terminals raise the insulation resistance reading
Loose terminals make the RCD trip faster than it should
Loose terminals overheat and can start a fire
Tight terminals are needed for the meter to work

questions.stem: Cables pass through a fire-rated wall between a hotel's kitchen and its corridor. What should the inspector check?
options: That the hole has been left open for cooling air
That the cables are painted the colour of the wall
That the cables pass through near the floor level
That the hole is sealed with suitable fire-stopping

questions.stem: On a hotel roof, PVC conduit carrying cables is in full sun. What should the inspector check?
options: That it is painted black so it absorbs the heat
That it is UV-resistant and properly supported
That it is buried under loose gravel on the roof
That it has no fixings, so it can expand freely

questions.stem: In a hotel bathroom, what does the inspector check about an outlet near the basin?
options: It has RCD (GFCI) protection and suits a wet area
It is the same colour as the bathroom's wall tiles
It is fitted inside the shower, where it is handy
It is wired on the room's lighting circuit

questions.stem: How should a defect be written up in an inspection report?
options: In a short code that only the inspector understands
As a general comment, such as 'the wiring is poor'
Only by word of mouth to the client's cleaner
Clearly: what and where, with its class and action

questions.stem: The client refuses to let you isolate a circuit with a dangerous defect. What should you do?
options: Isolate it anyway and lock the client out of the board
Explain the danger in writing and record the refusal
Leave without saying anything and send the bill later
Repair it live so that the client does not lose power

questions.stem: A circuit failed its insulation test, and the fault has now been repaired. What must happen next?
options: Repeat the tests on it and record the new results
Copy results from a similar circuit onto the schedule
Switch it on, since the repair must have fixed it
Leave it off the certificate and tell the client

questions.stem: When inspecting a new pump motor circuit, what should the inspector confirm about the overload relay's setting?
options: It is set at twice the motor's full-load current
It is set as low as it will go, so it trips often
It matches the full-load current on the nameplate
It is set to the maximum rating of the cable

questions.stem: At the end of the initial verification of a new clinic, what should the client receive?
options: A spoken promise that everything is in order
The tester's printout of readings and nothing else
The certificate, the schedules and the test results
The keys to the inspector's own padlocks

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What symbol is used for the part of the earth fault loop impedance that is outside the installation, measured at its origin?
In the result R1 + R2, what does R2 stand for?
Using I = U ÷ Z, how many amps of fault current flow if U is 110 V and Z is 0.55 Ω?
What are the parts of the work called that the inspector and client agree will not be covered, such as cables under fixed floors?
Two circuits each read 200 MΩ when tested alone. About how many megohms will they read when tested together?
What is the point called where the supply enters an installation, and where Ze is measured?
Which RCD test raises the test current little by little until the device trips, to show its actual trip current?
What is it called when only a part of the accessories is opened and checked, to stand for all of them?
What is the material called that seals holes where cables pass through a fire-rated wall?
In an IP rating such as IP65, which digit tells you the protection against water: the first or the second?
What is the switch called that stops a standby generator and the mains being connected to the house wiring at the same time?
What is the bonding called that joins incoming metal water and gas pipes to the main earthing terminal?
In inspection and testing, what do the letters PFC stand for?
Which document records the condition of an existing installation and any defects found, after a periodic inspection?
Which part of the verification uses mainly the eyes to check the installation, without test instruments?

essays.stem: Describe how you would plan the initial verification of a new two-storey house. Include the information you need, the team, the instruments and the order of the work.
essays.modelAnswer: First I collect the information: the drawings, the circuit schedule, the design data such as cable sizes and breaker types, and the expected Ze and maximum Zs for each circuit. I agree with the builder when the installation will be complete and free of other trades. I choose the team, for example myself as lead with two trainees, and give each a role: inspector, tester and recorder. I check that the instruments are in calibration, in good condition and suited to the work: two-pole tester and proving unit, low-resistance ohmmeter, insulation tester, earth electrode tester and, for later, the multifunction tester for live tests. I prepare blank schedules. The order of work is: safe isolation, with lock, tag and a proved tester; visual inspection of the whole installation; dead tests in order, which are protective and bonding conductor continuity, insulation resistance, polarity and the earth rod; then, only when these pass, a competent person energises and does the live tests and functional checks. Finally I complete the certificate and hand over.
markingPoints: Collects drawings, schedules and design data
Organises the team with clear roles
Checks instruments: calibration, condition, suitability
Gives the correct order: isolation, inspection, dead tests, then live tests by a competent person
Plans the paperwork and handover

essays.stem: Describe at least eight things you would check during the visual inspection of a new small hotel's installation, and say why each matters.
essays.modelAnswer: I check that cables are the right size for their breakers, so the breaker protects the cable from overheating. I check that breakers and RCDs are the right type and rating, and that RCD or GFCI protection is fitted to bathrooms, kitchens, outdoor and pool areas, where the risk of shock is higher. I check fittings in wet or outdoor areas have a suitable IP rating. I look for main bonding to incoming metal pipes, close to their entry, so metal parts cannot rise to a dangerous voltage. I check terminations are tight, with no bare copper showing, because loose joints overheat. I check boards have no open gaps and all covers are fitted, so live parts cannot be touched. I check cables are supported, protected from damage and sun, and kept apart from data cables. I look for fire-stopping where cables pass through fire walls. I check labels: circuit chart, warning notices and dual-supply labels. I check switches are in the line conductor, and that isolators for equipment such as air-conditioning units are in reach and marked.
markingPoints: Cable size matches protective device; correct device types and ratings
RCD/GFCI protection and IP ratings in wet or outdoor areas
Main bonding, terminations and no access to live parts
Cable support, protection and segregation; fire-stopping
Labels, notices and isolators, with a reason given for each check

essays.stem: Explain the steps of a periodic inspection of an occupied shop, from agreeing the extent and limitations to issuing the report.
essays.modelAnswer: I meet the shop owner and agree what will be inspected, what will not, such as cables hidden in walls, and the sample size of outlets to open. I write these down as the extent and limitations. I agree times to switch off circuits, so tills, freezers and computers are protected, and I find out about any alterations since the last report. I bring the previous report and drawings if they exist. On the day, I isolate each part safely: switch off, lock off, tag and prove dead with a tester checked before and after. I inspect the board and a sample of accessories, increasing the sample if I find faults. I do the dead tests on the circuits, then a competent person does the live tests such as loop impedance and RCD trip times. I record every reading. I class each defect by how serious it is, and I make safe and report at once anything dangerous. Finally I give an overall result, recommend the date of the next inspection, sign the report and explain it to the owner.
markingPoints: Agrees and records extent, limitations and sample size
Plans shutdowns with the client and gathers past records
Isolates safely and inspects, enlarging the sample when faults appear
Tests: dead tests, live tests by a competent person, all recorded
Classes defects, deals with danger at once, gives overall result, next date and explains the report

essays.stem: A circuit is 30 m long. The cable data gives 19.5 mΩ per metre for line plus protective conductor. Ze is 0.35 Ω, the maximum Zs for the breaker is 1.5 Ω, and the line-to-earth voltage is 110 V. Work out R1 + R2, the expected Zs and the earth fault current, and say whether the circuit is acceptable. Show your working.
essays.modelAnswer: R1 + R2 = 30 m × 19.5 mΩ per metre = 585 mΩ, which is 0.585 Ω. The expected Zs = Ze + (R1 + R2) = 0.35 + 0.585 = 0.935 Ω. The maximum allowed is 1.5 Ω. Because a cable gets hot in a fault and its resistance rises, a measured value taken cold is usually compared with a lower figure, for example about 80% of the maximum, which here is 1.2 Ω. 0.935 Ω is below both 1.2 Ω and 1.5 Ω, so the circuit is acceptable. The earth fault current is I = U ÷ Zs = 110 ÷ 0.935 = about 118 A. This is enough current to make the breaker trip quickly. If the measured R1 + R2 on site were much higher than 0.585 Ω, I would look for a loose or poor joint before accepting the result.
markingPoints: Zs = 0.935 Ω (about 0.94 Ω)
Compares with the maximum, allowing for temperature rise
Fault current about 118 A
States the circuit is acceptable and what a higher reading would mean

essays.stem: Explain the three classes of observation used in a periodic inspection report (danger present, potentially dangerous, improvement recommended). Give an example of each and say what the inspector must do.
essays.modelAnswer: Danger present means someone could be hurt now. An example is a broken outlet with live parts that can be touched, or a cable with bare conductors in reach. The inspector must tell the person in charge at once, make it safe with their agreement, for example by isolating the circuit, and record it. Potentially dangerous means it is not dangerous at this moment but would become so if a fault happened. Examples are a missing protective conductor to a metal fitting, no RCD on an outdoor outlet, or a breaker too large for its cable. These must be put right urgently. Improvement recommended means the installation does not meet the current standard but is not unsafe, for example an old circuit chart or a missing label. The client should plan to deal with it. Any danger present or potentially dangerous item makes the overall result unsatisfactory. Each observation is written clearly, with its location and the action needed.
markingPoints: Danger present: correct meaning and example
Action for danger: tell the client, make safe, record
Potentially dangerous: correct meaning, example and urgent action
Improvement recommended: correct meaning and example
Effect on the overall result and clear recording

essays.stem: Compare initial verification with periodic inspection. Cover the purpose, when each is done, how much is inspected and tested, and the document issued.
essays.modelAnswer: Initial verification is done on a new installation, or a new addition, before it is put into use. Its purpose is to prove that the work meets the design and the standard and is safe to switch on. Every circuit is inspected and fully tested: continuity, insulation resistance, polarity and earth electrode while dead, then loop impedance, prospective fault current, RCD and functional tests by a competent person. A certificate is issued, with schedules of inspection and test results, and signed for design, construction and testing. Periodic inspection is done on an existing installation at set intervals, or when a building changes hands or use. Its purpose is to find damage, wear, overloading or unsafe alterations. The extent and limitations are agreed first, and a sample of accessories may be opened, with the sample enlarged if faults are found. A condition report is issued that classes each defect, gives an overall result and recommends when the next inspection should be done.
markingPoints: Initial: new work, before use, to confirm design and safety
Initial: everything inspected and fully tested; certificate issued
Periodic: existing work, at intervals or change of use, to find deterioration
Periodic: agreed extent and limitations, sampling
Periodic: condition report with classed defects, overall result and next date

essays.stem: As lead inspector, you supervise two trainees testing a small clinic. Explain how you would organise the work, keep it safe and check their results.
essays.modelAnswer: Before we start, I brief the trainees on the job, the drawings and the order of work, and I give each a clear role, such as tester and recorder, swapping later. I agree with the clinic manager when each circuit can be off, because some equipment may be important to patients. I show them the safe isolation for each circuit: switch off, lock off with their own padlocks, tag and prove dead with a tester checked on a proving unit before and after. I check their instruments and leads first. I stay close while they test, especially during insulation tests, so nobody touches a circuit under test. I watch the method on the first circuits and correct mistakes early. When they record readings, I compare them with what I expect: for example, longer circuits should have higher R1 + R2. Results that look odd or too neat, I retest myself. Live tests are done only by me or another competent person. At the end I check the whole schedule, sign it, and talk through with the trainees what they did well and what to improve.
markingPoints: Briefs the team and gives roles
Plans shutdowns with the client
Ensures safe isolation and checks instruments
Supervises closely and checks results against expectations, retesting doubtful ones
Keeps live tests for a competent person; signs off and gives feedback

essays.stem: Describe what you would check when inspecting a house's standby generator connection and changeover switch, and why each check matters.
essays.modelAnswer: First I check that there is a proper changeover (transfer) switch, and that it cannot connect the generator and the mains at the same time. This stops the generator feeding back into the power company's lines, where it could kill a line worker, and stops damage when the mains returns. A generator must never be fed in through an ordinary outlet with a two-plug lead. I check that the changeover switch is rated for the full load current and switches the neutral where the design requires it. I check that the generator inlet and cable are of the right rating, protected and weatherproof. I check that the generator is earthed as the design and maker require. I check that the generator is placed outdoors, away from doors and windows, because its exhaust gives off carbon monoxide. I check that there are warning labels at the board saying there is more than one supply, and that the user knows how to change over safely. Finally the circuits are tested on both supplies by a competent person.
markingPoints: Proper changeover switch that prevents parallel connection, with the reason (back-feed danger)
No connection by a two-plug lead through an outlet
Ratings of switch, inlet and cable; weatherproofing
Earthing and safe generator position (carbon monoxide)
Labels, user instruction and testing on both supplies

essays.stem: Explain what main protective bonding is, what it connects, why it is needed, and how you would inspect and test it.
essays.modelAnswer: Main protective bonding joins metal services that come into the building, such as metal water pipes and gas pipes, and exposed structural steel, to the main earthing terminal. It is needed because, during an earth fault, these metal parts could be at a different voltage from each other or from earthed equipment. A person touching both could get a shock. Bonding keeps them at nearly the same voltage, so the risk is much lower. To inspect it, I check that a bonding conductor of the size given in the design is fixed to each service as close as practical to where it enters, using a proper clamp on clean metal, with a label warning that it must not be removed. I check that the conductor is not broken or damaged and is connected firmly at the main earthing terminal. To test it, with the installation isolated, I use a low-resistance ohmmeter with nulled leads between the main earthing terminal and each bonding clamp. The reading should be very low, a small fraction of an ohm, and I record it.
markingPoints: Defines main protective bonding and what it connects
Explains why: keeps metal parts at the same voltage in a fault
Inspection: size, position near entry, proper clamp and label
Test: low-resistance ohmmeter with nulled leads, installation isolated
Expects a very low reading and records it

essays.stem: Explain how the age of an installation, the Jamaican climate and the way a building is used affect what you look for during a periodic inspection. Give examples.
essays.modelAnswer: Older installations may have cable insulation that has gone brittle, few or no RCDs, missing protective conductors to lighting points and boards that no longer meet the standard. Over the years, owners often add circuits or air-conditioning units without upgrading the supply, so I check for overloading, heat marks and alterations done badly. The climate matters too. Near the coast, salt air corrodes metal boxes, conduit, clamps and terminals, so I look for rust and green corrosion. Strong sun breaks down plastic conduit and cable sheaths outdoors. Heavy rain and flooding let water into outdoor fittings and low boxes. After a hurricane, I look for damaged overhead cables, loose fixings and water in boards. Pests such as rats and termites can damage cables in roofs. The use of the building also matters: a hotel kitchen, a pool area or a workshop is harder on the installation than a quiet office, so I inspect these areas more closely and may recommend a shorter interval to the next inspection.
markingPoints: Age: deteriorated insulation, missing RCDs or protective conductors, out-of-date boards
Alterations and overloading added over time
Climate: salt-air corrosion, sun damage, water entry, hurricane damage
Pests and other local causes of damage
Use of the building affects focus and the next-inspection interval

practical1.title: Inspect and test a training installation bay and complete its certificate
practical1.brief: The assessor gives the group a training bay wired as a small apartment: a distribution board, a lighting circuit, a 110 V outlet circuit, a 220 V water-heater circuit, a bathroom outlet with RCD (GFCI) protection, a metal water pipe with main bonding, and an earth rod if the Centre has one. The bay is NOT connected to any supply. The assessor has planted defects, such as a breaker too large for its cable, a missing blank in the board, a fitting with the wrong IP rating, a loose bonding clamp and a switch in the neutral. As a group, plan the verification and give each member a role (lead inspector, inspector, tester, recorder), swapping so that everyone tests. Isolate and lock off the bay's supply point with every member's padlock and a tag, and prove dead with a tester checked before and after. Carry out a full visual inspection on the schedule of inspections. Then carry out the dead tests: continuity of the main bonding and of each protective conductor (R1 + R2), insulation resistance, polarity and, if fitted, the earth rod. Work out the expected R1 + R2 from the cable data given, add the Ze the assessor gives you to find each Zs, and compare it with the maximum figures given. Complete the schedule of test results and the certificate, marking the live tests 'to be done by a competent person', and list every defect with the action needed.
materials: Training installation bay with planted defects, not connected to any supply
Two-pole voltage tester and proving unit
Low-resistance ohmmeter or insulation and continuity tester, and earth electrode tester if a training earth rod is fitted
Lock-off kit, a padlock for each member and tags
Cable resistance data, Ze and maximum Zs figures (from the assessor)
Blank schedule of inspections, schedule of test results and certificate
Calculators, torch and hand tools for opening accessories
photos: The group's written plan with roles
The supply point locked off with every member's padlock and a tag
The tester being checked on the proving unit before and after proving dead
Each planted defect, with a label showing the group's finding
A protective conductor continuity test at the far end of a circuit
An insulation resistance test in progress
The calculations of R1 + R2 and Zs
checklist: Helped plan the work and kept to their role
Isolated, locked off and proved dead correctly, with the tester checked before and after
Inspected their part of the bay against the schedule and found defects
Carried out at least one continuity and one insulation test correctly, with leads nulled
Worked out R1 + R2 and Zs correctly and compared them with the maximum
Recorded readings and defects clearly and accurately
Explained the action needed for each defect they found
Left the bay and tools safe and tidy
safety: The bay is never connected to a supply during this task; live tests are only written up, not done
Every member fits their own padlock before any cover is removed
Warn others before each insulation test and let the circuit discharge before touching it
Use only test leads and probes in good condition

practical2.title: Carry out a periodic inspection of an older training installation and write the condition report
practical2.brief: The assessor sets up a training rig as an older shop installation, NOT connected to any supply, with signs of wear and alterations: a corroded box, a cracked accessory, an added air-conditioning circuit with an oversize breaker, a missing circuit chart, an outdoor outlet with no RCD and a loose terminal. The assessor plays the shop owner. As a group, first meet the 'owner' to agree the extent, the limitations and the sample of accessories to open, and write them down. Then isolate and lock off the rig with every member's padlock and a tag, and prove dead with a tester checked before and after. Each member inspects a part of the rig and opens accessories from the sample, enlarging the sample if faults are found. Carry out dead tests on a sample of circuits. The assessor gives a card with the live test results a competent person took (Ze, Zs and RCD trip times): compare them with the limits given. Class every defect as danger present, potentially dangerous or improvement recommended, with its location and action. Complete the condition report with an overall result and a recommended date for the next inspection, then present it to the 'owner' and answer their questions.
materials: Training rig set up as an older shop installation, not connected to any supply
Card of live test results and limits (from the assessor)
Two-pole voltage tester and proving unit; insulation and continuity tester
Lock-off kit, a padlock for each member and tags
Blank agreement sheet for extent and limitations, and a blank condition report
Hand tools, torch, camera or phone
photos: The agreed extent and limitations, signed by the 'owner'

checklist: Took part in agreeing the extent, limitations and sample
Isolated and proved dead correctly, with the tester checked before and after
Inspected their part of the rig and enlarged the sample when faults were found
Classed each defect they found correctly and gave a sensible action
Compared the live test results with the limits and drew the right conclusions
Helped give the right overall result and next inspection date
Explained findings to the 'owner' clearly and politely
safety: The rig is never connected to a supply during this task
Every member fits their own padlock before any cover is removed
Treat corroded or cracked parts with care: wear gloves and safety glasses
Live tests are not done by trainees: their results come from the assessor's card
